driver: The decisive quantity is a forward projection for a group as constituted on the projection date, so every past period of its history has to be rebuilt on that membership; joining each period's records to the membership in force in that period, the point-in-time build that history work normally demands, books past changes of membership as growth or shrinkage and moves the projection, upward for groups that absorbed members and downward for groups that shed them.
driver_concrete: The limit-monitoring standard projects each obligor group's 31 December 2026 exposure as its 30 September exposure plus its average quarter-on-quarter change over the four quarters to 30 September, for the group as it stands on the projection date; groups on the agenda took control of borrowers the bank already lent to and sold others during the year, so rebuilding each quarter on the GLEIF snapshot archived at that quarter-end turns membership changes into exposure trend, while the projection the standard wants restates every quarter on the 30 September 2026 hierarchy, predecessor LEIs carried to their successors.
stump: A competent solver joins each quarter's loan, securities and derivative extracts to the GLEIF snapshot the bank archived at that quarter-end, the point-in-time build that keeps later knowledge out of a history, so the requesting group's acquisition of a borrower the bank already lent to enters its history as quarter-on-quarter growth, its projected year-end exposure is overstated and it approves less of the request than the limit allows (names and figures fixed at build).
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms every quarter's three books correctly (lapsed registrations kept, branches to head office, fund-management links not followed, merged LEIs to successors, ISIN fallback for blank issuer LEIs) and reads the standard correctly builds each past quarter on the hierarchy archived for that quarter, because point-in-time joins are the default discipline for history, and so books membership changes as exposure change and files the wrong approvable amount, too low for a group that grew by acquisition and too high for one that sold a borrower.
domain_test: The call turns on credit-exposure aggregation to obligor groups under accounting-consolidation control across drawn loans, undrawn commitments, securities and derivative replacement cost, checked against house limits through a limit-monitoring projection; with another field's nouns the consolidation hierarchy, the commitment exposure measure and the limit framework have nothing to attach to.
